text: PRE-REGISTERED (plan 515be79a7d12). 16 peptide-receptor complexes, Boltz-2 + DockQ. All three hypotheses CONFIRMED. Overall CAPRI-acceptable rate 0.625, median DockQ 0.36, median fnat 0.518.

LEAKAGE SIGNAL, large and unambiguous. Pre-cutoff complexes (which Boltz could have memorised) reach 7/8 = 0.875 acceptable with median DockQ 0.8725; post-cutoff reach 3/8 = 0.375 with median DockQ 0.18. That is a 0.50 drop in success rate and a 4.8x drop in median DockQ. Unlike study #6, which was underpowered, this effect is large enough to see at n=8 per stratum.

ipTM IS WELL CALIBRATED for this task: Spearman rho(ipTM, DockQ) = 0.8471, p = 3e-05. The band confusion against AlphaFold3's published interpretation bands: 9 confident-and-acceptable, 1 confident-but-wrong, 4 in the failed band and wrong, and ZERO in the failed band that were actually acceptable. So ipTM < 0.6 produced no false negatives here, and ipTM > 0.8 was wrong once in ten. This is the first calibrated interpretation key this project has for any confidence metric.

GATE FOR STUDY #9: OPEN. The pipeline recovers 7 of 8 memorisable interfaces, so it has demonstrated sensitivity and a screen of unknown candidates can in principle detect a true binder. Study #9 may therefore run as a positive screen rather than only as a negative control. The calibration above supplies its interpretation key: the platform's own candidates scored ipTM 0.21-0.47 in the earlier pilot, which falls in the band where 4 of 4 complexes here were wrong.

DECLARED DEVIATION and a harness bug it exposed. The registered plan specified an explicit DockQ chain mapping; DockQ's own chain search was used instead. Measured: on 4XHV `--mapping AB:AB` raises KeyError('A') inside DockQ while the identical files score DockQ 0.899 when DockQ chooses the mapping, and the same explicit form works on 4XOJ. The first run of this study recorded 4XHV and 4XOE as failures when they are in fact 0.899 and 0.279 — the harness was discarding correct results. Selected mappings are now recorded and verified against the expected one.

DEPENDENCY ISOLATION. DockQ 2.1.3 hard-pins numpy<2 while this project's scipy/pandas/prodigy stack requires numpy>=2; installing DockQ silently downgraded numpy to 1.26.4 and left scipy emitting an out-of-range warning while still importing. Rather than compromise either side, DockQ was isolated in .venvdockq and is invoked as a subprocess. A statistics library running outside its supported numpy range is exactly the kind of silent corruption this project exists to prevent.

task: withdraw the ipTM-well-calibrated claim (audit finding 4; ret_0003)

text: CORRECTED, AND IT WITHDRAWS clm_4775b69b2b653295. ipTM RANKS interface quality on this set: Spearman rho(ipTM, DockQ) = 0.800, p = 2e-04, n = 16. That is discrimination over a batch of 16 complexes, not a calibrated confidence scale and not a per-complex filter. Two independent corrections made inside this study produced it. (a) THE VALUE: DockQ had silently scored 10TC against native chain H, a 4-residue copy of the curated 8-residue peptide; under the curated chain mapping that entry falls from DockQ 0.969 to 0.831 and the correlation moves from 0.847 to 0.800 (data/study_peptide_interface.json, analysis.metrics.spearman_iptm_dockq = 0.8, analysis.spearman_p = 0.0002). (b) THE WORD: Spearman is invariant under any strictly monotone transform, so replacing ipTM by ipTM squared leaves rho and p untouched while moving 3 of the 10 entries out of the >0.8 band (4Y29, 4Y32, 23AG) -- the statistic cannot see the rescaling that the band thresholds depend on. What survives: the absolute bands, as a much smaller piece of evidence -- 9 confident-and-acceptable, 1 confident-but-wrong, 4 failed-band-and-wrong, zero failed-band-but-acceptable, plus 1 grey-and-acceptable and 1 grey-and-wrong -- where the zero rests on 4 observations. And the CONFIRMED verdict on H2_iptm_calibration, whose registered criterion was rho > 0.6 with p < 0.05: the threshold did fire, at the corrected value. Withdrawn claim held once in the retraction ledger as ret_0003.

note: rho 0.8471 -> 0.800 after the 10TC chain-mapping correction, and 'calibrated' -> 'ranks/discriminates'. ret_0003.

rationale: The value and the word are withdrawn; the verdict is not. THE WORD: Spearman is invariant under any strictly monotone transform -- ipTM squared leaves rho and p untouched while moving 3 of the 10 entries out of the >0.8 band -- so it measures discrimination, not calibration, and this project holds no calibrated confidence scale for any metric. NOT withdrawn: the band confusion (9 confident-and-acceptable, 1 confident-but-wrong, 4 failed-band-and-wrong, zero failed-band-but-acceptable, on 4 failed-band observations), and the CONFIRMED verdict on H2_iptm_calibration, whose registered criterion was rho > 0.6 with p < 0.05.
